value: FTC FCRA Disposal Rule, Telemarketing Sales Rule, FTC Act Section 5; Federal Communications Commission (FCC) TCPA calling restrictions for call centers (47 CFR 64.1200); Consumer Financial Protection Bureau / FTC FCRA employment background-check rules; DHS / USCIS Form I-9 retention for employers and recruiters/referrers for a fee; PHMSA (DOT) Hazmat security plans for waste haulers transporting listed hazardous materials; HHS OCR HIPAA for call centers and staffing firms acting as business associates

NAICS 56 is heterogeneous (staffing/PEO, call centers, security guards, facilities services, waste) and has no sector-specific federal cyber mandate. CSF 2.0 gives one outcome-based baseline onto which the binding pieces can be mapped: FCRA/Disposal Rule for background data, HIPAA BA duties, PCI DSS for payment-taking call centers, FAR 52.204-21 for government facility-service contractors. For payment-heavy call centers, use PCI DSS v4.0.1 as the gap target instead.

SSNs, I-9 identity documents, work authorization data; Background check / consumer reports (FCRA); Payroll, bank account and tax withholding data (PEOs); Benefits enrollment and group health plan PHI; Payment card data captured by call centers; Call recordings and biometric time-clock data; Customer site access credentials (security guard/janitorial firms)

Applicant tracking systems (ATS) and VMS; Payroll / HCM / PEO platforms; Contact-center (CCaaS), IVR and call-recording platforms; Workforce management and time & attendance (incl. biometric clocks); Guard tour / access control and CCTV systems; Fleet routing/telematics and scale-house systems (waste)

NYC Local Law 144 (AEDT bias audits) NYC Local Law 144 of 2021 Bias audit, public summary and candidate notice before using automated employment decision tools.; Colorado SB26-189 (ADMT in consequential decisions) Colo. SB26-189 Covers employment decisions; applies to staffing/PEO deployers of ADMT affecting Colorado consumers.

Solid waste collection and remediation have no CISA sector-specific cyber rule. The Water and Wastewater Systems Sector covers wastewater utilities (NAICS 22), not NAICS 562. Biometric time clocks can trigger state biometric privacy laws (e.g., Illinois BIPA, 740 ILCS 14). The Illinois site could not be fetched (HTTP 503), so BIPA specifics are unverified. All 50 states, DC and the territories have breach notification statutes with differing triggers, deadlines and regulator-notice duties. They are not enumerated here.
